Constants preserved: DYNAMIC_MARK = 'data-dynamic-app-icon' (L14) and FALLBACK_BG = '#0a0a0f' (L20) kept; DYNAMIC_MARK is surfaced in the published snapshot (dynamicMark) since React Native has no DOM <link>/<meta> nodes to tag, and FALLBACK_BG is used as the manifest background_color (web L140). The big file-level JSDoc L9-50 (Layer 1 favicon + data-base-href/useFaviconBadge coordination, Layer 2 apple-touch-icon, Layer 3 manifest, theme-color meta) is reproduced in the native header and on the hook JSDoc, adapted to the native snapshot-store model.

@/lib/appIcon helpers inlined faithfully: buildAppIconSvg (web appIcon source) ported verbatim incl. VIEWBOX=200, RX_STANDARD=44, BOLT_PATH, safeHex regex guard, and the apple (full-bleed, no rx), maskable (translate(20 20) scale(0.8) safe-zone), and standard (rx) SVG variants used at L66/L96/L114-115. svgToDataUrl (web appIcon L107-127) reimplemented with a self-contained ASCII base64 encoder (encodeBase64Ascii) instead of the browser btoa, which Hermes does not ship, so the data: URL is byte-identical on device and under Jest (Node); the web's `typeof btoa !== 'function'` empty-string guard is rendered moot by the local encoder. renderSvgToPngDataUrl (web appIcon L129-164) has no <canvas>/Image on native so it resolves null — exactly the web hook's documented jsdom/headless skip path (DYNAMIC_APP_ICON_PNG_UNAVAILABLE_REASON).

Hook signature export function useDynamicAppIcon(): void (L51) kept exactly. State preserved verbatim: const { theme } = useTheme() (L52); lastBlobUrlRef = useRef<string|null>(null) (L53); lastSignatureRef = useRef<string>('') (L54). Effect deps [theme.primary, theme.accent] (L167) unchanged. The L56-63 signature dedup (primary=theme.primary, accent=theme.accent, signature=`${primary}|${accent}`, early-return when unchanged, then store the new signature) is byte-faithful; the L57 `typeof document === 'undefined'` guard is replaced by the native publish path documented inline (no document on RN).

Layer mapping (DOM injection -> observable snapshot publish): L65-79 Layer 1 favicon (buildAppIconSvg standard -> svgToDataUrl -> set on every link[rel=icon] + data-base-href + DYNAMIC_MARK) -> compute faviconSvg + faviconHref and publish them as faviconSvg/faviconDataUrl/baseHref/dynamicMark. L81-91 theme-color meta (create-if-absent + set content=primary + DYNAMIC_MARK) -> publish themeColor=primary. L93-106 Layer 2 apple-touch-icon (renderSvgToPngDataUrl(appleSvg,180).then(dataUrl => if(!dataUrl) return; set href on link[rel=apple-touch-icon])) -> same fire-and-forget structure preserved with `void renderSvgToPngDataUrl(appleSvg,180).then`; native raster -> null so the `if (!dataUrl) return` skip fires exactly as on the web when canvas is unavailable, with a signature-guarded in-place patch of appleTouchIconPng for any future native raster.

L108-166 Layer 3 manifest ported with identical control flow: Promise.all([render std 192/512, maskable 192/512]) then `if (!std192 || !std512 || !msk192 || !msk512) return` (web L125) — native raster yields all-null so this skip fires, faithful to the web's explicit jsdom/sandboxed-iframe skip comment (L123-124). The manifest object literal (web L135-150: name/short_name/start_url/display/background_color=FALLBACK_BG/theme_color=primary/orientation/categories=['auto','utilities']/icons[4]) is published synchronously as DynamicAppIconManifest with every metadata field intact and the 4 icon entries (192/512 any + 192/512 maskable, type image/png) preserved with src=null (PNG raster unavailable). The Blob + URL.createObjectURL link swap (L152-164) is unavailable on native (DYNAMIC_APP_ICON_DOM_UNAVAILABLE_REASON); lastBlobUrlRef + the previous-blob revoke ordering (L157-165) are mirrored — lastBlobUrlRef is set on raster success and `previous` is read before publish — but stay inert on native since raster never succeeds.

L169-179 unmount cleanup ported verbatim in shape: a second useEffect with [] deps returns a teardown reading lastBlobUrlRef.current and, if set, performing the native blob-revoke analog (publishDynamicAppIcon(null)) then nulling the ref. Because native raster never succeeds, lastBlobUrlRef stays null and the teardown is a no-op — exactly matching the web hook in a canvas-less (jsdom) environment, where only the manifest blob is revoked while the favicon/meta survive — so the published snapshot persists after unmount.

Rule 7 explicit unavailable state: two exported reasons document the browser-only gaps — DYNAMIC_APP_ICON_DOM_UNAVAILABLE_REASON (no document/favicon/apple-touch-icon/<meta theme-color>/<link manifest>/Blob/URL.createObjectURL to inject into) and DYNAMIC_APP_ICON_PNG_UNAVAILABLE_REASON (no <canvas>/Image rasterizer). The computed brand intent is surfaced via an observable in-process store (subscribeDynamicAppIcon / getDynamicAppIconSnapshot) emitting a DynamicAppIconSnapshot (signature, primary, accent, faviconSvg, faviconDataUrl, baseHref, dynamicMark, themeColor, appleSvg, appleTouchIconPng, standardSvg, maskableSvg, manifest, pngIconsAvailable) for a native brand surface (header mark, status-bar tint, splash icon) to consume. __resetDynamicAppIconForTests clears the snapshot + subscribers for clean test runs — the useCriticalAlertFlash precedent.

Gates from apps/native all pass after the change: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit) clean; npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint) clean; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles green. Baseline was green before the change; the new hook is brand-new and imported by nothing yet, so no existing test/behavior is affected.
